nodes.description: Intravenous pamidronate lowers severe hypercalcaemia and halts skeletal demineralisation before parathyroidectomy, and serves as rescue therapy. It does not lower PTH. Reported single doses are 0.5 to 1 mg/kg.

nodes.description: Cinacalcet binds the calcium-sensing receptor allosterically and raises its sensitivity to extracellular calcium. In this disease the drug can only act on whatever mutant receptor reaches the cell surface and still signals, so its effect depends on the alleles: in transfected cells calcimimetics restore signalling of several disease mutants, and fail on mutants that are not expressed at the surface. The relation to the other nodes is pharmacological compensation for the receptor defect, not causation, so this node asserts no downstream edge.

An oral calcimimetic used off-label. It acts on the receptor itself, so it needs mutant receptor that reaches the cell surface and can still signal. Reported outcomes range from years of control on cinacalcet alone to no response at all. Infants with one inactivating allele respond more consistently than infants with two, and among biallelic cases the response follows the alleles: missense variants with residual function have responded, while a deletion-frameshift and a conformation-locking missense variant have not. Because the result cannot be predicted reliably, several authors propose a short trial while genetic results are awaited. Reported doses were titrated against calcium and PTH, from 0.5 mg/kg/day up to 8.5 mg/kg/day in two or three divided doses.

nodes.description: Loss of the receptor in the renal tubule raises the renal calcium threshold, so calcium is reabsorbed despite hypercalcaemia and urinary calcium is low. After total parathyroidectomy the same defect persists, which is the explanation offered for falling calcium and calcitriol requirements in long-term follow-up. In Casr-deficient mice the hypocalciuria survives removal of the parathyroids or of PTH, so the defect is renal and independent of PTH. The tubular segment (thick ascending limb) and the claudin effectors come from mouse and FHH1 work and have not been shown in NSHPT, which is why the node stays provisional.

nodes.description: Serum calcium far above the neonatal range, characteristically above 15 mg/dL, presenting in the first days to weeks of life. The non-specific features of neonatal hypercalcaemia (hypotonia, poor feeding, constipation, polyuria, dehydration, lethargy, failure to thrive) follow from it. That those features are caused by the hypercalcaemia, rather than by PTH or bone disease directly, is drawn from the general neonatal hypercalcaemia literature, not from NSHPT-specific studies.

nodes.description: The definitive treatment, performed once calcium has been lowered medically. All four glands are removed, and because supernumerary and ectopic glands occur some surgeons add transcervical thymectomy. Whether to autotransplant parathyroid tissue is unsettled: in the largest series almost every infant, autotransplanted or not, ended up on calcium and vitamin D, and other surgeons avoid autotransplantation because of graft-dependent recurrence. Surgery is followed by hungry bone syndrome and usually by permanent hypoparathyroidism. It removes the parathyroid limb of the disease only; the renal calcium retention persists.
